messages:
anya: running long-window bring-up for v3-quant (8-bit PTQ) and seeing small but reproducible token drift after ~18k tokens. not full collapse, just next-token probs shift on repeated prefix.
anya: repro script: `python tests/long_context/check_kv.py --model v3-quant --seq 25000 --seed 42 --prompt-file tests/long_context/prompt_a.txt`
anya: attached a short excerpt of the log where token 18204 deviates:
```
[18202] token=... 'the' p=0.21
[18203] token=... 'cat' p=0.14
[18204] unquant= 'sat' p=0.12 | quant= 'sits' p=0.11
```
anya: behavior looks like a tiny phase shift rather than catastrophic forgetting. repeated across 3 seeds.
raf: can you run the same on `v3-fp16` to rule out model topology vs quantization? also which quant backend (q4_0/q4_1) and quantizer config?
anya: yes ran fp16 earlier — no divergence up to 25k tokens. quant backend is q4_1 with per-channel scales, fused rotary tables enabled.
raf: ok that points to quantization interaction with RoPE/kv storage. maria: fwiw we saw something vaguely similar with older quantizer where sin/cos interp lost precision at high positions — wrap/aliasing shows as a small phase offset.
maria: question: are you using position ids that keep incrementing or resetting for cache? if caching accidentally reuses a shorter position id space you can see aliasing.
anya: using absolute position ids (pos += len(chunk)) and never resetting. cache stores (layer, key, pos) tuples.
sam: can you paste the kv hash diff check? even a single-layer mismatch would highlight storage corruption vs transformation mismatch.
anya: here's the quick diff we run at the end of infer batch: `for l in layers: assert np.allclose(kv_q[l], kv_fp[l], atol=1e-3)` — fails only after token ~18k for keys in layers 10..14
raf: try comparing raw KV dot-product results rather than keys: `K@Q.T` for the affected positions. if keys quantized cause small projection error it will manifest there.
anya: doing that now. also switching quant backend to q4_0 to see if symmetric quant helps.
anya: quick update: K@Q mismatch grows with position index; plotting phase of complex rotary encoding (sin/cos projected) shows a linear drift.
maria: that suggests either quant rounding on the rotor embedding or the rotor tables are being recomputed with float16 and then quantized separately (two different pipelines). double-check the table generation code path for quant build.
anya: TIL: the quant build reuses precomputed rotary tables saved as fp32 but then we re-quantize them during model export. going to try freezing the tables to the same dtype before export.
raf: good. also try a cheap mitigation in serving: clamp position ids when pos>max_window to use aliasing intentionally (i.e., pos % period) and see if deterministic alias reduces drift vs incremental overflow. if drift is from mismatch between expected and actual aliasing behavior you'll see change.
anya: interesting idea — will test.
deploy-bot: deploy started: model/v3-quant/freeze-rotary-tables -> staging (id: dpl-20260320-67).
ops-bot: note: staging GPU hosts have slightly different cudnn versions; if you get non-determinism across hosts run the check on a single pinned host.
anya: confirmed deterministic on pinned host. freezing rotary tables removed the linear phase drift in our run. need to run full battery (stress with varied prompts and seq lengths).
sam: nice. once you have full battery, please open an eval run with that artifact and add a short README for the quant export step so onboarding engineers don't reintroduce this.
anya: will do. adding test that compares frozen-table-quant vs fp16 up to 30k tokens. also adding a quick note to docs: `quantization/export.md` about locking rotary table dtype.
maria: we should also add a microbench that computes phase error vs position for each quant backend and include it in Optimize recommendations. could save future debugging time.
anya: adding to backlog and will PR a new eval. thanks all :thumbsup:
